newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica fx controls could have gone in '95 - Manuel.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica fx controls could have gone in '95 - Manuel.

text.p: South Africa may have missed an opportunity a year ago to lift foreign exchange controls or at least accelerate the process, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said in an interview published on Thursday.
The minister told Business Report that the country was getting towards the desirable level of reserves of around three months import cover at the end of 1995.
But even before that level had been reached there may have been scope for more decisive action.

"I think that if I were in this position 12 months ago, with eight or nine weeks' cover and a sense of pressure, perhaps, yes, I would have been emboldened to act differently," said Manuel, who took over as finance minister in March 1996.

Manuel said he understood comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals last week that removing exchange controls on residents might take up to five years, but he preferred not to put a time frame on the process.
"It has got to be determined by a confluence of a number of factors that are evaluated rather than some date," he said.
